text:
24-hour news summary.

1. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (https://t.me/dlmehr/5635) was awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.
2. Suleyman argued (https://t.me/dlmehr/5636) that Claude’s uncertainty about consciousness reflects Anthropic’s training choices rather than evidence of actual consciousness.
3. Hugging Face introduced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5637) an open-source proxy that turns unmodified coding harnesses into RL environments, improving LFM2.5-2.6B performance across multiple harnesses.
4. TestingCatalog reported (https://t.me/dlmehr/5638) that Figure may launch its proactive AI assistant Hark this week with multimodal models, memory, projects, scheduled tasks, computer use, and paid plans.
5. Reka announced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5639) Rho-1, a 19-billion-parameter omni model capable of processing and generating text, images, video, and robot actions.
6. Mark Levine warned (https://t.me/dlmehr/5640) that AI-exposed entry-level job postings in New York City have fallen sharply since 2022.
7. OpenAI announced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5641) optional global text watermarking for select API models, with invisible watermarks coming to ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU.
8. Sam Altman recounted (https://t.me/dlmehr/5642) seeing Andrew Garfield impersonate him outside his home during filming for “Artificial.”
9. Nolla Health reportedly became (https://t.me/dlmehr/5643) the first U.S. organization approved to let an AI issue initial prescriptions, creating an end-to-end AI doctor.
10. Banbury Road AI introduced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5645) Kardashev-0.7, a 32-model RL-trained swarm designed to achieve frontier performance with substantially lower inference cost and memory.
11. Ghost AI introduced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5646) Core, described as a personal AI computer, and began taking orders.
12. OpenAI reportedly optimized (https://t.me/dlmehr/5647) default response speed by about 50% for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol across its subscription products and partner services.
13. Liquid AI announced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5648) vision-enabled d1, a fast decision model that reportedly matches or beats GPT-6.1 Sol on four of six applications at 19–200 times lower cost.
14. Stanford highlighted (https://t.me/dlmehr/5649) Karl Deisseroth sharing news of his Nobel Prize with his children.
15. Cognition introduced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5650) Devin’s Dreaming feature, which builds and refines a cross-session memory graph, alongside an open Agent Memory Repo standard.
16. Skull8888888888 introduced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5651) flow-1, an RL-trained model for detecting errors in agent traces that reportedly matches GPT-6 Sol at 23 times lower cost.
17. Sharon Lee described (https://t.me/dlmehr/5652) a robotics simulation approach combining affordance modeling, physics calibration, and real-world trajectories for more meaningful policy signals.
18. Reason Machines launched (https://t.me/dlmehr/5653) Reason 1.0, a lightweight coding agent offering customization for users’ models and subscriptions.
19. Epoch AI reported (https://t.me/dlmehr/5654) that OpenAI researchers’ coding-agent spending doubled approximately once per month from January through mid-August 2026.
20. Kairos introduced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5655) Kairos 1, a model designed to simulate individual human behavior and reportedly outperform several competitors across 13 benchmarks.
21. Reflection AI announced (https://t.me/dlmehr/5656) Beam, an open model with 501 billion total parameters and 23 billion active parameters, with full weights due this month.
22. Andreessen Horowitz published (https://t.me/dlmehr/5657) its seventh Top 100 Consumer AI Apps ranking, noting ChatGPT’s continued lead, Claude’s rise, and expansion into coding, music, design, voice, video, agents, and hardware. (1/2)
